title: Iridescent Material Transfer Studio
description: The user operates a material experimentation studio where a glass vase with flowers sits beside an iridescent abalone shell. Through a multi-step workflow, the user extracts iridescence properties from the abalone, tunes parameters like iridescence intensity, thickness range, and base color tint, then applies the hybrid material onto the glass vase to create a fantastical iridescent flower vase.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive material transfer studio. Load GlassVaseFlowers.glb on the left and IridescenceAbalone.glb on the right of the scene, both on a reflective dark platform. Use a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 1.5, 4) looking at origin. Add an HDR-style lighting rig: one warm DirectionalLight from upper-left, one cool DirectionalLight from upper-right, and a soft AmbientLight. Add OrbitControls with damping. Build a floating HTML control panel (top-right, semi-transparent dark background) with these sequential interaction steps: Step 1: A button labeled 'Extract Iridescence' that visually pulses the abalone shell (scale animation) and enables the next controls. Step 2: A slider for 'Iridescence Intensity' (0.0 to 1.5, default 1.0, step 0.05) — validate range. Step 3: A slider for 'Iridescence Thickness Min' (100 to 400nm, default 100, step 10). Step 4: A slider for 'Iridescence Thickness Max' (400 to 800nm, default 400, step 10) — validate max > min. Step 5: A color picker for 'Base Color Tint' that blends with the original glass material color. Step 6: A slider for 'Metalness Blend' (0.0 to 1.0, default 0.3). Step 7: A button labeled 'Apply to Vase' that animates a glowing particle trail from the abalone to the vase (use a simple animated sphere traveling along a bezier path), then applies MeshPhysicalMaterial with the configured iridescence parameters to all vase meshes. Step 8: A 'Reset' button that reverts the vase to its original materials with a fade transition. Display a step indicator showing progress (e.g., 'Step 3/8'). Disable controls for future steps until prior steps are completed. All parameter changes after application should live-update the vase material. Ensure transmission is set to 0.3 on the final vase material to retain partial glass appearance.
